```plato
//==
// # Solids
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Solids — parametric surfaces for the solids
//  - The typed polyhedral solids as polygon meshes
//  - Deformation bodies for the profile-generated solids

library Solids
{
    //==
    // # Solids — parametric surfaces for the solids
    //
    // The parametric boundary surface of each solid, as the IParametricSurface
    // obligations. Solids are centered at the origin with Z as the up axis in their
    // local frame; UV is in [0,1]x[0,1]: U wraps around the Z axis (ClosedU is true
    // for every solid), V runs up the shape (or around it, for the torus). Polygonal
    // solids walk their profile at constant rate with flat sides (linear between
    // vertices), so a UV quad grid meshes them exactly.
    //
    // Every solid carries its own placement, so the local-frame convention above
    // describes the solid's LOCAL frame and the local point is mapped to world at
    // the end of each body — through the type's own `Frame` where it has one,
    // through its `Orientation` quaternion where it has one, and otherwise through
    // `AxisFrame`, which manufactures a stable (but arbitrary) frame around a
    // `Center`/`Axis` pair. The UV seam therefore lands at an arbitrary azimuth for
    // the Center/Axis solids, which is all a seam needs; nothing downstream may
    // assume where it is.
    //
    // Because U always wraps and V (except the torus) does not, the matching face
    // grid is `AllQuadFaceIndices(nCols, nRows, true, false)` from
    // `meshes.library.plato` — the "flat sides, constant rate" clause is what
    // makes that grid mesh the polygonal solids EXACTLY rather than approximately.

    //==
    // Shared profile helpers

    // The point at `radius` from the origin in direction `a`, in the XY plane.
    PointOnCircle(a: Angle, radius: Number): Point2D
        => (a.Cos * radius, a.Sin * radius);
```
